doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Met orchestra and joining CTI
title: Crying Song, the Gary McFarland date and guitarist Sam Brown
summary: Brown dates Crying Song to September 1969. Laws identifies a garbled name in the discography as guitarist Sam Brown.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Then we get to Crying Song. Crying Song is September 1969.

Memphis. That’s what you referenced earlier in this interview, about being called for that one. So that brings us up to date on that and at least gets us to there. Here we go. What’s showing up now is Gary McFarland, September ’69, Curtis Fuller on
trombone, you, Gary McFarland on vibes and vocal, George Ricci, cello, Sam Brown, guitar, Ron Carter and Chet Amsterdam, and then Grady Tate and Sol Gubin, and then Airto.
Did you remember you mentioned Sam Brown earlier? You said his name was Bluch or something on that other record.
Guitar. They blew it. That’s Sam Brown. That’s the same guy, played the guitar on my record.
I don’t know if he was under contract, but one of the things we found out from Kenny was he had to use an alias because of contractual restrictions.
So he had changed his name on a couple. Then he didn’t realize that he was actually on that session, because he didn’t recognize his name.

You know what? I don’t think Sam Brown had that problem, because he wasn’t signed to any label. But he was a fine guitarist. He played both electric and acoustic guitars. He used to be on all the sessions. Every time you’d go, you’d see Sam playing on those sessions.
